name: jet-a
prompt: Photorealistic studio product render of a modern large-cabin long-range business jet (Dassault Falcon 6X class, but a generic design of our own), isolated on a fully transparent background. Strict orthographic plan view from DIRECTLY ABOVE, no perspective, no tilt, nose pointing STRAIGHT UP to the top edge, perfectly mirror-symmetric left and right about the vertical centre line, centred, the aircraft filling about 86 percent of the frame height. Accurate real-aircraft proportions: a long slender cylindrical fuselage (length slightly greater than the wingspan, fuselage width about one tenth of the length), a long pointed elegant tapered nose with a dark tinted wraparound cockpit windscreen, a row of small oval cabin windows barely visible along each side of the cabin; low wings mounted at about mid fuselage, swept back about 34 degrees, thin and tapered with a slim chord at the tips, ending in small upswept winglets; NO engines under the wings: exactly two slim cylindrical engine nacelles mounted on short pylons on either side of the REAR fuselage, just ahead of the tail; a cruciform tail with a swept vertical fin and small swept horizontal stabilisers. Finish: glossy pearl white paint, clean, with very subtle soft panel shading and a few faint fine panel seams, dark grey wing walkway and leading edge tone barely visible, soft studio lighting from the top left with smooth gradients and a gentle specular sheen along the fuselage spine, giving true volume. Slightly stylised and pristine, a soft premium friendly feel, like an Apple product render. No shadow, no background.

name: jet-b
prompt: High-end 3D product render, like a hero image Apple would make, of a sleek twin-engine business jet seen exactly from above in orthographic top-down plan view, nose straight up, perfectly bilaterally symmetric, centred on a fully transparent background, filling about 86 percent of the frame height. Real aircraft proportions of a Falcon 6X class large-cabin jet (not a replica, no branding): long slender fuselage, sharp but softly rounded pointed nose, black glossy cockpit windscreen at the front, tiny cabin windows along both upper sides of the fuselage; thin wings swept 34 degrees with a straight trailing edge kink near the root, slender tips with small winglets; clean wings with nothing under them; two slender engines on pylons at the rear of the fuselage on both sides, their round intakes facing forward; swept T-tail with a slim horizontal stabiliser at the top of the fin. Glossy white paint, subtle cool grey shading on the sides, faint panel lines, a soft specular highlight along the top of the fuselage and the wing roots, studio key light from the upper left. Clean, realistic, refined, very slightly stylised. Nothing else in the image.

name: jet-c
prompt: Ultra-clean realistic render of a large-cabin business jet as an app icon hero object, top-down orthographic plan view from directly above, nose pointing straight up, symmetric left and right, isolated on a fully transparent background, filling about 86 percent of the frame height. Design: an elegant long-range business jet in the spirit of the Falcon 6X: long slim fuselage with a long pointed aerodynamic nose cone; dark smoked cockpit windshield; very small round cabin windows along the top edges; slender wings swept back 34 degrees, tapered, with gently upturned winglets; two rear-fuselage-mounted turbofan engines in slim nacelles beside the tail cone (and absolutely no engines on the wings); cruciform tail with a tall swept fin seen edge-on from above as a thin line, and swept horizontal stabilisers at mid fin height. Glossy white automotive paint, soft grey ambient occlusion where wings meet the fuselage, very subtle panel lines, smooth studio reflections, light from the top left. Precise, refined, premium and friendly. No shadow, no background.

name: jet-d
prompt: Top-down view of a private business jet, scale-model photography quality: a perfect, pristine 1:48 display model of a large-cabin long-range business jet with a glossy white finish, photographed straight down from directly above with an orthographic look, nose pointing straight up, the model perfectly symmetric, isolated and cut out on a fully transparent background, filling about 86 percent of the frame height. Correct proportions of a real jet like a Falcon 6X: long slender fuselage, long pointed nose with a dark cockpit glass, small cabin windows along the sides, slim 34 degree swept wings with small winglets, two engines mounted on the rear fuselage next to the tail, nothing under the wings, swept T-tail. Soft diffused studio light from the upper left, gentle highlight on the top of the fuselage, subtle soft shading, very faint panel lines. No stand, no shadow, no background.
